issue:
HTML pages for the jobs (server-rendered, no JavaScript)

The JSON API works for tools; people want a page to look at. Add server-rendered HTML pages to the same FastAPI app
(ledger/api.py, `create_app(jobs_dir)`), built with the standard library only (no template engine, no JavaScript, no
external CSS or fonts).

1. GET /ui: an HTML page with a table of the jobs, oldest first, one row per job with the job id, state, number of
   stages and cost ("$0.2826"), and "running" for a job that /jobs marks running. Each job id is a link to its page. Under
   the table, the totals: "<n> jobs, $<total>" as on the summary. With no jobs, the page says "No jobs." instead of a table.
2. A filter by state: GET /ui?state=REVIEW_READY shows only the jobs in that state, and the totals are for the shown jobs.
   Above the table there is one link per state present in the directory (with its count), and a link "all" to /ui.
   An unknown state shows "No jobs." (not an error).
3. GET /ui/jobs/{job_id}: the page of one job: its id, state, created_at, cost, and a table of its stages in order (stage,
   kind, status, cost), and a link back to /ui. An unknown or invalid job id: 404 with an HTML page that says
   "no such job: <id>" and links back to /ui. The same id rules as /jobs/{job_id} (never a path outside the directory).
4. Every value from job.json is HTML-escaped (a state or id containing "<script>" must appear as text, never as markup).
5. Responses are `text/html; charset=utf-8`; the JSON endpoints and `python -m ledger summary` do not change.

The numbers must be the ones the JSON API gives (reuse it; do not compute costs a third way). Tests use TestClient and
html.parser from the standard library: they read the table cells and follow every link on a page (each must answer 200,
except the deliberate 404). Add a short "Pages" section to README.md. Environment: ledger_py312.
